subject: Your storage clock starts at the written notice not at the landing
body:
The same clock runs at all seven bush stations and the notice is what fixes its start date. Past three days from that notice you can bill 75 cents a hundredweight a day. The study below builds that date off the on hand count Bethel's already running daily.

https://alaskaaihq.com/awesomeproposal/ryan-air/

Worth a reply or a forward either way.

Talon at Alaska AI
title_note: Published by Ryan Air for media, community and donation requests, corroborated independently by info.lynden.com which renders the address in clear as a live mailto alongside five other named carrier contacts. She is NOT the buyer. Lee Ryan, President, is the decision-maker and no address for him is published anywhere fetchable, so the email is written to be forwarded and names nobody.
opens_on: Their own freight rules give three days after WRITTEN NOTIFICATION of arrival before storage fees may be applied at $.75 per 100 pounds or part thereof per day, so the notice date is what both the free window and the fee hang on, across all seven bush stations.
lead_critic: ship on round 3. Round 1 was killed for misstating their own tariff in the first sentence, stating a permissive fee as automatic and deleting the three day window, plus a chiasmus that presupposed a records failure we had explicitly refused to verify, naming their President to someone in external communications, and a construction Talon has hand-rewritten on three separate sends. Round 2 fixed all of that and left two defects, the body's opener restating the subject almost word for word, and a boundary drift claiming the fee a day earlier than the tariff allows. Round 3 moved the seven stations onto the operational claim they actually support and corrected the boundary to past three days.
